    OPEN THE BLACK BOX

    A useful model.
    Not a promise.

    Illustrative shot patterns use a historical PGA TOUR distance-and-lie cost reference. This teaches tradeoffs; it does not predict your personal score.

    How shots are generated

    Basic training uses a straight, centered Gaussian shot pattern. Handicap sets an illustrative training bag: driver total-distance limits are 280 yd (scratch), 265 yd (5), 250 yd (10), and 225 yd (20). These are profile limits, not measured averages or universal personal maximums. Approach shots allow up to the profile’s 3 wood. Left/right comes from the main view; the depth bar changes depth along that aim line. The target specifies intended carry. After you choose a target, a short line and hollow finish marker show planned straight-line rollout before curve or random misses. Zoom in for a closer view. This planning aid does not reveal dispersion or the recommended target. After a normal practice shot, white markers show the core center flight landing and finish; water contact stops its rollout. Zero-roll shots use one location. The shortest estimated club that can carry that distance is selected, then club-specific rollout determines its planned finish. Core σ scales by intended carry divided by that club’s stock carry capacity. The table below shows the current profile’s full-swing assumptions. These are illustrative presets, not measured handicap averages. Member preview uses your saved club distances, shapes and miss settings. The shortest club that can carry to the target is selected automatically. Core σ, curve, usual bias and big-miss offsets scale by intended carry / stock carry, with a 25% floor; start angle, height and big-miss probability stay fixed. Driver is excluded for approaches; stock distance uses saved carry, with zero rollout. Custom curve and bias may move the mean finish away from the nominal target. Club carry accepts 50–330 yd and rollout 0–40 yd.

    80% of core shots lie within ±1.282σ on each individual axis; a joint 80% ellipse is larger (radius 1.794σ). The core contour is shown only after you commit. The blue comparison uses the same player and club-selection rules at the best sampled aim. Member big misses use a mixture component with twice the core σ plus the configured directional shift and carry loss.

    How decisions are scored

    Next-shot costs use Mark Broadie’s historical PGA TOUR benchmark (2003–2010), with separate distance curves for fairway, rough, sand, recovery and putting. A 150 yd fairway shot has a 2.945-stroke reference; sand at 20 yd has 2.53, versus 2.82 at 40 yd. These are reference-player values, not your personal expected score. Handicap changes your simulated shot pattern. The comparison shows the extra expected cost of your target against the best sampled target, rather than official strokes gained for a real shot.

    We estimate one stroke + penalties + strokes remaining. Lower is better. We compare direction and depth using a broad grid (6 yd left/right, 10 yd short/long), then refine near its best target in 2 yd steps. Search covers each hole’s aiming range (normally 60 yd left to 60 right; sharp doglegs allow 120 yd each side) within each hole’s depth range, and includes your selected target. Basic targets obey the same distance limit and automatic club model; dispersion changes with club and distance. Member targets use the same saved bag and the same distance-scaling rule. The best sampled target is an approximation, not a proven global optimum.

    Quick feedback: “strong decision” means within 0.05 expected strokes of the best sampled target. “Too aggressive” means water, OB, bunker or tree exposure is more than 2 percentage points higher (or all shots are OB). “Too conservative” means the nominal mean is over 5 yd farther from the pin without that extra exposure. Other cases say “target needs refining” so we do not force a misleading label.

    Score = max(0, 100 − 60 × extra expected strokes). A score of 100 requires a target within 2 yd of the best sampled target and within 0.005 extra expected strokes. Other nearly equal choices are capped at 99. The comparison is approximate; a 100 is not a guaranteed good shot.

    Green front/back yardages are measured along the ball-to-green-center line; flag yardage is the direct distance from the ball. Tap the decision rating after commitment to open a lesson with the actual hazard rates, proximity, club and target adjustment behind the recommendation. Member-preview progress stores the latest 1,000 attempts on this device. Trends use first attempts only, with separate profiles when shot or scoring assumptions change; retries remain separate. Varied hole difficulty means these trends are practice feedback, not a measured real-world skill improvement.

    Comparisons use the same 4,000 random draws. Approximate ±95% Monte Carlo error covers sampling noise only, not uncertainty in these assumptions.

    What hazards cost

    OB: stroke and distance. A shot plus a one-stroke penalty returns you to the original spot; the same strategy is repeated in the expectation calculation.

    Water: one penalty stroke plus remaining strokes from a fixed, scenario-specific drop location. This is a simplified relief assumption.

    The animated array shows 48 evenly spaced examples from the 4,000 scored shots. Colors describe their final outcomes; the exact percentages come from all 4,000. Flight arcs and camera motion are illustrations, not a physics model. Dispersion dots use the same outcome colors as the tracers. Your dots are filled; comparison dots are hollow. Solid gold and dashed blue outlines identify the two 80% core contours.

    Practice uses fourteen authored hole families with seeded variations, rather than a fixed list to choose from. Par-5 second shots include an open green and a forced water carry, with layup depths available. They appear in Approach and Mixed practice and use the same approach club limits (no driver or rollout). Tee / Approach / Mixed filters control Next shot. Mixed favors the other shot type and avoids recently used families when possible. Next shot varies width, length and safe pin position; doglegs can bend left or right. Geometry moves together so the view and scoring stay aligned. Retry this hole keeps the exact layout and random sample.

    Water is checked at carry and during roll. Wooded corridors vary independently on each side in setback, density, start distance and visual height. Dense woods use a higher modeled recovery cost than open woods. These are endpoint recovery zones inside the white stakes; tree height does not affect airborne shots. Vegetation beyond the stakes remains OB. Woodland, Pacific Coast, desert and mountain settings vary the scenery on these layouts. Mountain peaks and evergreen trees are visual only. Lakeside and oceanfront settings appear on layouts with an existing scored side-water hazard; distant water scenery is outside the playable hole. The elevated view places tee shots 9 m and approaches 8 m above their landing areas while retaining a 1.7 m eye height above the ball. Raised greens, sunken bunkers and pond banks add illustrative surface relief, exaggerated for readability. The exposed hazard bowls are a visual teaching aid. Aim points, pins and tracer contacts follow those surfaces while hazard footprints and outcome scoring remain in the same 2D yard coordinates. This is visual terrain only: downhill carry, wind, slope-dependent roll and airborne tree contact are not modeled.

    Current basic training bag

    Adjust this to your own typical driver reach. It rescales club distances; each handicap keeps its dispersion profile. Settings save for each handicap. This applies to the free handicap profile. Member preview uses its separate saved club distances.

    Estimated clubStock totalRolloutCore σ side / long

    Stock distances: Driver 100%, 3 wood 89%, Hybrid 78%, 5 iron 71%, 6 iron 66%, 7 iron 58.5%, 8 iron 53%, 9 iron 47.5%, PW 41.5%, SW 30% of the driver limit. Woods / hybrid use 100% / 82% / 66% of driver σ; irons use the profile’s 155-yard approach σ × stock distance / 155. Requested carry below stock carry scales σ proportionally, with a 25% floor. Member preview lets you replace these estimates with your own club distances and miss settings. No measurements are inferred from dragging the flight.

    Adjust the strokes-remaining model

    Optional adjustments to the historical Tour reference. Zero recovery adjustments use the source tables directly. Handicap changes shot dispersion, not the reference golfer’s recovery or putting skill. Older custom cost settings reset for this new baseline.

    Default next-shot costs interpolate Broadie’s historical PGA TOUR tables by distance and lie: fairway, rough, sand, recovery and green. Putting uses feet; other distances use yards. Published off-green values start at 10 yd and end at 600 yd; putting uses a 1 ft tap-in anchor and published 2–90 ft values. Outside those ranges we use the nearest endpoint. Tree density scales the recovery cost above fairway. Custom offsets alter this reference and are not measured handicap data.

    MY SHOT PROFILE

    Create your custom shot

    Match the flight to the shot you usually hit—not your best shot. If your ball usually finishes right of where you aim, move the blue finish right of the target. Practising with your usual flight helps you learn where to aim so your shots finish in a safer place.

    Your ball flight

    Red apex: drag left/right to shape the start and bend; drag up/down for height.
    Blue finish: drag left/right to move the finish while keeping your start line.

    Limits: 10° either way for start; 50 yd either way for bend.

    WhenShotScoreRating

    Trends compare first attempts under the same shot profile and scoring assumptions. Changing the handicap, distance limit, personal bag or scoring costs creates a separate profile. Retrying the same scenario does not enter the trend, even after a reload or settings change. Hole difficulty varies, so a rising score is practice feedback rather than proof of improvement on the course. These are simulated decisions, not your real handicap or strokes gained.
